package.name: Encoding
package.description: Hexadecimal, Base64, Base32, Base58 and percent-encoding of byte sequences

modules.name: Base32
modules.header:
Base32 in the RFC 4648 alphabet and in Douglas Crockford's.
Every five bytes become eight characters of five bits each. The RFC 4648 alphabet, `A` through `Z` then `2`
through `7`, is what one-time-password secrets and many file systems that ignore case use, padded with `=` to a
multiple of eight characters. Crockford's alphabet drops `I`, `L`, `O` and `U` so that a human reading an
identifier aloud or typing it back cannot confuse two characters, and it never pads.
Both read either case. Crockford decoding also does what its specification asks of a reader: `I` and `L` are read
as `1`, `O` as `0`, and hyphens, which a human may insert to group the characters, are skipped. That leniency is
part of that alphabet's contract and does not extend to the RFC form, which is read strictly, unused trailing
bits included.
The RFC form runs in time that depends only on the length, through the arithmetic in `Digits.rux`. Crockford's is
meant for identifiers rather than secrets and maps characters with an ordinary table. The whole text is checked
before a byte is written, so a refusal leaves the destination exactly as it was.

modules.name: Base58
modules.header:
Base58 in the Bitcoin alphabet, which leaves out `0`, `O`, `I` and `l` so that no two characters look alike.
Unlike the power-of-two bases, Base58 does not split bytes into fixed groups of bits. The whole input is one big
number written in base 58, so every output digit depends on every input byte and the work grows with the square of
the length; the scheme is meant for short values such as keys, hashes and addresses. Each leading zero byte is
written as a leading `1`, because a number has no leading zeros to keep.
The conversion works in the destination itself, digit by digit, rather than in a separate buffer, so it needs no
allocation and no size limit. The cost is the capacity refusal: by the time the destination proves too short it
has been used as scratch space, so a refusal leaves it zeroed rather than untouched. Every other refusal is
found before anything is written. Base58 is not constant time and should not carry a secret whose timing matters.

modules.name: Base64
modules.header:
Base64 in the two alphabets RFC 4648 defines, each with and without padding.
Every three bytes become four characters of six bits each. The standard alphabet ends in `+` and `/`; the URL-safe
one in `-` and `_`, so its output can sit in a URL or a file name unescaped. Padding with `=` rounds the text up
to a multiple of four, which the standard form requires and the URL-safe form usually leaves out.
Decoding is strict, as section 3.5 of the RFC permits: no whitespace, no line breaks, no characters from the other
alphabet, padding exactly where the variant puts it and nowhere else, and the unused low bits of the last
character zero. Each of those rules is one way two different texts could otherwise decode to the same bytes, and
a decoder that is one-to-one is one whose output can be compared as text.
Both directions run in time that depends only on the length, through the arithmetic in `Digits.rux`. The whole
text is checked before a byte is written, so a refusal leaves the destination exactly as it was.

modules.name: Digits
modules.header:
The digit arithmetic behind the hexadecimal, Base64 and Base32 alphabets, computed without branches or tables.
These encodings carry keys, tokens and secrets as often as anything else. A decoder that branches on each
character, or indexes a table with it, takes time and touches cache lines that depend on the secret, which is
enough to recover it from a co-resident process. So every function here maps a value to its digit, or a digit to
its value, with masks built from arithmetic alone. Each range test is `((low - 1 - c) & (c - (high + 1))) >> 8`,
which is all ones when `low <= c <= high` and zero otherwise, because both differences are negative only inside
the range and the shift is arithmetic on a signed value.
The inputs are a single byte widened to `int32`, so none of the differences can overflow. Validity is still
reported to the caller, which then branches on it: whether a text is well formed is not a secret, and the caller
stops at the first invalid character anyway.

modules.name: Error
modules.header:
Why text could not be decoded, shared by every scheme in this package.
One error type for five schemes, because the ways decoding fails are the same everywhere: a character outside the
alphabet, a length the scheme cannot produce, padding in the wrong place, bits the encoder would never have set,
or a destination too short for what the text holds. A caller that accepts several encodings handles one type.
Every input failure carries the zero-based byte offset into the text it was given, so a caller can point at the
character rather than reject the whole string. The capacity failure carries the length the destination needed
instead, which is the number a caller sizing a buffer actually wants.

modules.name: Hex
modules.header:
Base 16: two digits per byte, the high nibble first, as RFC 4648 section 8 defines it.
Encoding writes one case, lower unless asked otherwise, and decoding reads both, because the two mean the same
thing and hexadecimal arrives in whichever case its producer liked. Nothing else is accepted: no `0x` prefix, no
separators and no whitespace, since a decoder that skips characters is one whose input two systems can read
differently.
Both directions run in time that depends only on the length, through the arithmetic in `Digits.rux`, so a key or
a token can pass through them without its value showing in the timing. Every function checks the room it needs
before it writes a byte, so a refusal leaves the destination exactly as it was.

modules.name: Percent
modules.header:
Percent-encoding, as RFC 3986 defines it for URIs and HTML defines it for submitted forms.
A byte that may not appear literally in some part of a URI is written as `%` and two upper-case hexadecimal
digits. Which bytes those are depends on the part, so the encoder takes a set: a single component such as one
query value or one path segment keeps only the unreserved characters, a whole path also keeps `/` and the
characters a path may carry, and a form keeps fewer still and writes a space as `+`.
Decoding turns every valid escape back into its byte and leaves every other character alone. Characters that an
encoder would have escaped are accepted as they are, because text arrives from many encoders and a decoder that
refused them would refuse most of the web; an escape that is malformed is refused, because guessing what it meant
is how two decoders come to disagree. Escapes may decode to bytes that are not UTF-8, so the result is bytes.
Both directions check the room they need before writing, so a refusal leaves the destination exactly as it was.

modules.name: Stream
modules.header:
Encoding and decoding streams: a writer that turns the bytes written to it into hexadecimal, Base64 or Base32 text
on another writer, and a reader that turns such text from another reader back into bytes.
Both work a group at a time — one byte for hexadecimal, three for Base64, five for Base32 — through the same
functions that encode and decode whole slices, so a stream's output is exactly what encoding the whole input at
once would give. A writer holds back the bytes of an incomplete group until more arrive or `Finish` ends the text
with its last group and padding; a reader holds back an incomplete group of characters until the source ends.
Base58 has no streaming form, since every character depends on the whole input.

items.name: Base32Variant
items.signature: pub enum Base32Variant

doc.summary: Which Base32 alphabet a text uses, and whether it is padded.
doc.markdown:
Which Base32 alphabet a text uses, and whether it is padded.
Copy, carrying no payload.

cases.name: Standard
cases.doc: The RFC 4648 alphabet, `A` through `Z` then `2` through `7`, padded with `=` to a multiple of eight characters.

cases.name: StandardUnpadded
cases.doc: The RFC 4648 alphabet without padding, which is how one-time-password secrets are usually written.

cases.name: Crockford
cases.doc:
Crockford's alphabet, `0` through `9` then the letters except `I`, `L`, `O` and `U`, without padding. Read
leniently, as its specification asks: either case, `I` and `L` as `1`, `O` as `0`, and hyphens skipped.

items.name: Base32EncodedLength
items.signature: pub func Base32EncodedLength(length: uint, form: Base32Variant) -> uint

doc.summary: How many characters the Base32 form of `length` bytes occupies in `form`.
doc.markdown:
How many characters the Base32 form of `length` bytes occupies in `form`.
Eight characters for every five bytes, with a final partial group taking two, four, five or seven characters,
or eight with padding. Cannot fail for any length a slice in memory can have; runs in constant time and
allocates nothing.

params.markdown: the number of bytes to encode

params.name: form
params.markdown: the alphabet and padding to encode with

doc.summary: Writes `bytes` as Base32 into `into`.

Letters are written in upper case in both alphabets. The RFC 4648 variants run in time that depends only on the

`Base32EncodedLength(bytes.length, form)`, leaving it exactly as it was; room past the encoded form is not
touched.

params.name: into
params.markdown: the destination, at least `Base32EncodedLength(bytes.length, form)` characters

params.name: form
params.markdown: the alphabet and padding to encode with

items.name: Base32DecodedLength
items.signature: pub func Base32DecodedLength(text: char8[..], form: Base32Variant) -> uint ! DecodeError

doc.summary: How many bytes the Base32 text decodes to, after checking its length and the placement of its padding.
doc.markdown:
How many bytes the Base32 text decodes to, after checking its length and the placement of its padding.
Only the shape is checked; the characters are checked by `Base32Decode`. The padded variant needs a multiple of
eight characters; every variant needs the data characters to leave a final group of zero, two, four, five or
seven. Hyphens in Crockford text are not counted. Reports `InvalidLength` at the end of the text, or
`InvalidPadding` at the first `=` that is out of place. Runs in time linear in the length and allocates nothing.

params.name: form
params.markdown: the alphabet and padding the text is expected to use

doc.returns: the number of bytes `Base32Decode` writes for it

items.name: Base32Decode
items.signature: pub func Base32Decode(text: char8[..], into: var byte[..], form: Base32Variant) -> uint ! DecodeError

doc.summary: Reads Base32 text in `form` into `into`.
doc.markdown:
Reads Base32 text in `form` into `into`.
The RFC 4648 variants run in time that depends only on the length of `text` when the text is valid. Reports, in
this order of precedence, `InvalidLength` or `InvalidPadding` for a text of the wrong shape, `InvalidCharacter` at
the first character outside the alphabet, `NonCanonical` at a last character whose unused bits are not zero, and
`InsufficientCapacity` with the length needed when `into` is too short. Every refusal leaves `into` untouched,
because the whole text is checked before anything is written.

params.name: into
params.markdown: the destination, at least `Base32DecodedLength(text, form)` bytes

params.name: form
params.markdown: the alphabet and padding the text is expected to use

items.name: Base58EncodedMaxLength
items.signature: pub func Base58EncodedMaxLength(length: uint) -> uint

doc.summary: The most characters the Base58 form of `length` bytes can occupy.
doc.markdown:
The most characters the Base58 form of `length` bytes can occupy.
Each byte needs at most log 256 / log 58, about 1.366, digits, so this is a bound rather than the exact length,
which depends on the value. A destination of this length is always enough. Cannot fail for any length a slice
in memory can have; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

params.name: length
params.markdown: the number of bytes to encode

doc.returns: an upper bound on the number of characters `Base58Encode` writes

items.name: Base58Encode
items.signature: pub func Base58Encode(bytes: byte[..], into: var char8[..]) -> uint ! FormatError

doc.summary: Writes `bytes` as Base58 into the front of `into`.
doc.markdown:
Writes `bytes` as Base58 into the front of `into`.
Runs in time quadratic in the length of `bytes`, and not in constant time. Reports `InsufficientCapacity` when
the encoded form does not fit `into`; `Base58EncodedMaxLength(bytes.length)` characters always fit. A refusal
leaves `into` filled with zero bytes, because the conversion used it as scratch space. Room past the encoded form
is not touched on success.

doc.markdown:
Writes the bytes of `text` as Base58 into the front of `into`.
The byte form, reached without the caller reinterpreting the text first: each UTF-8 code unit is one byte.
The failure the byte form reports, with the same guarantee.

items.name: Base58Decode
items.signature: pub func Base58Decode(text: char8[..], into: var byte[..]) -> uint ! DecodeError

doc.summary: Reads Base58 text in the Bitcoin alphabet into the front of `into`.
doc.markdown:
Reads Base58 text in the Bitcoin alphabet into the front of `into`.
Each leading `1` becomes a zero byte. Runs in time quadratic in the length of `text`, and not in constant time.
Reports `InvalidCharacter` at the first character outside the alphabet, leaving `into` untouched, and
`InsufficientCapacity` when the decoded value does not fit `into`, leaving it filled with zero bytes because the
conversion used it as scratch space. The count carried by that refusal is a lower bound on the length needed,
not the exact length; `text.length` bytes are always enough.

items.name: DecodeError
items.signature: pub variant DecodeError

doc.summary: Why text could not be decoded.
doc.markdown:
Why text could not be decoded.
Failure-only: success is the other channel of `uint ! DecodeError`, so no case means that nothing went wrong.
Copy, carrying one count and owning nothing. A decoder that reports any case except `InsufficientCapacity` has
left its destination exactly as it was; see each decoder for what a capacity refusal leaves.

cases.name: InvalidCharacter
cases.doc: A character that is not in the scheme's alphabet. The offset is that character.

cases.name: InvalidLength
cases.doc:
The text has a length no encoder of this scheme produces, such as an odd number of hexadecimal digits. The
offset is the text's length, where the missing character would have gone.

cases.name: InvalidPadding
cases.doc:
A padding character where padding is not allowed: in the middle of the text, too much of it, or any of it in
a scheme without padding. The offset is the first padding character that is out of place.

cases.name: NonCanonical
cases.doc:
The last character carries bits the encoder would have left zero, so two different texts would decode to the
same bytes. The offset is that character. Refusing it keeps decoding one-to-one, which is what makes an
encoded value safe to compare as text.

cases.name: InvalidEscape
cases.doc: A percent sign that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits. The offset is the percent sign.

cases.name: InsufficientCapacity
cases.doc: The destination is shorter than the decoded value. The count is the length it needed, in bytes.

doc.summary: Where in the text the failure was found, or none for a destination that was too short.
doc.markdown:
Where in the text the failure was found, or none for a destination that was too short.
Borrows the error and leaves it untouched. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
doc.returns: the zero-based byte offset into the text, or none for `InsufficientCapacity`

members.name: WriteDisplay
members.signature: pub func WriteDisplay(self: &DecodeError, writer: &var TextWriter, spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError

doc.summary: Writes a short lower-case description, followed by the offset or the length needed.
doc.markdown:
Writes a short lower-case description, followed by the offset or the length needed.
The text is `invalid character at 5` for an input failure and `destination too short, need 12 bytes` for a
capacity failure. No style is understood. Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for
a style.
doc.returns: success when the whole description was accepted

members.name: WriteDebug
members.signature: pub func WriteDebug(self: &DecodeError, writer: &var TextWriter, spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError

doc.summary: The same text as `Display`: the description already names the case and its count.
doc.markdown:
The same text as `Display`: the description already names the case and its count.
The failures `WriteDisplay` reports.
doc.returns: success when the whole description was accepted

items.name: PercentSet
items.signature: pub enum PercentSet

doc.summary: Which characters percent-encoding leaves as they are.
doc.markdown:
Which characters percent-encoding leaves as they are.
Copy, carrying no payload. Every set leaves the unreserved characters of RFC 3986 alone, apart from `Form`, which
escapes `~` as HTML requires.

cases.name: Component
cases.doc:
Only the unreserved characters: letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_` and `~`. Right for a single query name or
value, a single path segment, or any value placed between delimiters, since every delimiter is escaped.

cases.name: Path
cases.doc:
The unreserved characters, the sub-delimiters `!$&'()*+,;=`, and `:`, `@` and `/`. Right for a whole path
that is already split into segments the way it should be.

cases.name: Form
cases.doc:
The `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` serialization: letters, digits, `*`, `-`, `.` and `_` stay, a space
becomes `+`, and everything else is escaped. Decoding in this set reads `+` as a space.

items.name: PercentEncodedLength
items.signature: pub func PercentEncodedLength(bytes: byte[..], set: PercentSet) -> uint

doc.summary: How many characters the percent-encoded form of `bytes` occupies in `set`.
doc.markdown:
How many characters the percent-encoded form of `bytes` occupies in `set`.
Exact rather than a bound: one character for each byte the set leaves alone, or for a space in the form set,
and three for every other byte. Runs in time linear in the length and allocates nothing.

params.name: set
params.markdown: which characters stay as they are

items.name: PercentEncodedLength
items.signature: pub func PercentEncodedLength(text: char8[..], set: PercentSet) -> uint

doc.summary: How many characters the percent-encoded form of the bytes of `text` occupies in `set`.
doc.markdown:
How many characters the percent-encoded form of the bytes of `text` occupies in `set`.
The byte form, reached without the caller reinterpreting the text first: each UTF-8 code unit is one byte.

params.name: text
params.markdown: the text whose bytes to encode

params.name: set
params.markdown: which characters stay as they are

items.name: PercentEncode
items.signature: pub func PercentEncode(bytes: byte[..], into: var char8[..], set: PercentSet) -> uint ! FormatError

doc.summary: Writes `bytes` percent-encoded for `set` into `into`.
doc.markdown:
Writes `bytes` percent-encoded for `set` into `into`.
Escapes use upper-case digits, which RFC 3986 says producers should. Reports `InsufficientCapacity` when `into`
is shorter than `PercentEncodedLength(bytes, set)`, leaving it exactly as it was; room past the encoded form is
not touched.

params.name: into
params.markdown: the destination, at least `PercentEncodedLength(bytes, set)` characters

params.name: set
params.markdown: which characters stay as they are

items.name: PercentEncode
items.signature: pub func PercentEncode(text: char8[..], into: var char8[..], set: PercentSet) -> uint ! FormatError

doc.summary: Writes the bytes of `text` percent-encoded for `set` into `into`.
doc.markdown:
Writes the bytes of `text` percent-encoded for `set` into `into`.
The byte form, reached without the caller reinterpreting the text first: each UTF-8 code unit is one byte, so a
character outside ASCII becomes one escape per byte of its UTF-8 form, as URIs require.
The failure the byte form reports, with the same guarantee.

params.name: text
params.markdown: the text whose bytes to encode

params.name: into
params.markdown: the destination, at least `PercentEncodedLength(text, set)` characters

params.name: set
params.markdown: which characters stay as they are

items.name: PercentDecodedLength
items.signature: pub func PercentDecodedLength(text: char8[..]) -> uint ! DecodeError

doc.summary: How many bytes percent-encoded text decodes to, after checking that every escape is well formed.
doc.markdown:
How many bytes percent-encoded text decodes to, after checking that every escape is well formed.
Each `%` followed by two hexadecimal digits of either case counts as one byte, and every other character as one.
Reports `InvalidEscape` at the first `%` that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits. Runs in time linear in
the length and allocates nothing.
doc.returns: the number of bytes `PercentDecode` writes for it

items.name: PercentDecode
items.signature: pub func PercentDecode(text: char8[..], into: var byte[..], set: PercentSet) -> uint ! DecodeError

doc.summary: Reads percent-encoded text into `into`, turning each escape back into its byte.
doc.markdown:
Reads percent-encoded text into `into`, turning each escape back into its byte.
Characters outside an escape are copied as they are, except that `+` becomes a space when `set` is `Form`; the
other sets give `+` no special meaning. Reports `InvalidEscape` at the first `%` that is not followed by two
hexadecimal digits, and `InsufficientCapacity` with the length needed when `into` is too short; both leave `into`
untouched, because the whole text is checked before anything is written.

params.name: set
params.markdown: the set the text was encoded for, which decides how `+` is read

items.name: EncodingWriter
items.signature: pub struct EncodingWriter

doc.summary: A writer that encodes what is written to it onto another writer.
doc.markdown:
A writer that encodes what is written to it onto another writer. Not copied.
The text is complete only once `Finish` has written the last group and its padding.

members.name: New
members.signature: pub func New(sink: Writer, codec: StreamCodec) -> EncodingWriter

doc.summary: A writer encoding with `codec` onto `sink`.
doc.markdown: A writer encoding with `codec` onto `sink`.

doc.summary:
Ends the text: encodes the bytes of an incomplete last group, with padding where the form uses it, and
flushes the writer underneath.
doc.markdown:
Ends the text: encodes the bytes of an incomplete last group, with padding where the form uses it, and
flushes the writer underneath. Nothing more may be written afterwards.
doc.returns: nothing, or why the writer underneath failed

members.name: Write
members.signature: pub func Write(self: &var EncodingWriter, bytes: char8[..]) -> uint ! IoError

doc.summary: Encodes `bytes`, writing every complete group and holding back the rest of an incomplete one.
doc.markdown: Encodes `bytes`, writing every complete group and holding back the rest of an incomplete one.
doc.returns: how many were taken, which is all of them, or fails with `InvalidInput` after `Finish`

doc.summary: Flushes the writer underneath.
doc.markdown:
Flushes the writer underneath. An incomplete group stays held back, since its characters depend on bytes
not yet written; `Finish` is what writes it.
doc.returns: nothing, or why the writer underneath failed

items.name: DecodingReader
items.signature: pub struct DecodingReader

doc.summary: A reader that decodes text from another reader into bytes.
doc.markdown:
A reader that decodes text from another reader into bytes. Not copied.
The text is held to the same rules as the slice decoders, so text that would not decode whole fails with
`InvalidInput` when the reader reaches it. Crockford Base32 skips its hyphens, as its specification asks.

members.signature: pub func New(source: Reader, codec: StreamCodec) -> DecodingReader

doc.summary: A reader decoding `codec` text from `source`.
doc.markdown: A reader decoding `codec` text from `source`.

doc.markdown: Decodes into `into` as many bytes as are ready, reading more text when none are.
doc.returns:
how many were decoded, or fails with `EndOfStream` after the last, or with `InvalidInput` for text
